commit_note: The immutable commit containing this manifest and spec is supplied in the author's final handoff; a manifest cannot contain its own Git commit hash.
summary: Proposed local-first ptest NG product specification, with shared local admission, conservative selection, static doctor and explicit probes, resource ownership guidance, portable configuration, CLI/JSON semantics, TUI support tiers, negative contracts, and finite release gates. No detailed architecture or implementation is approved by this draft.
decisions: Bare ptest requests automatic local selection with full fallback; explicit scopes stay explicit and --full remains the authoritative configured gate.
Coordinate same-host/same-OS-user invocations across repositories, worktrees, shells, and TUIs, with conservative admission, fairness, cancellation, and ownership-aware crash recovery.
Propose Linux and macOS v1 support; pytest/Vitest are first-class, Go/Cargo retain bounded explicit execution, and arbitrary wrappers have explicit best-effort limitations.
Selection must account for dirty/untracked/configuration changes and unresolved failures; uncertain evidence widens execution and cannot fabricate a pass.
Static doctor never executes repository code; bounded probes are separately explicit; repair prompts are local data for an existing agent.
Use generic DB/cache/resource ownership recipes, reusable expensive setup, clean per-test state, factories/builders, and observed timing without a universal service-management framework.
Use ordinary noninteractive CLI, versioned JSON, one generic guide, and optional thin TUI pointers; no model API, launcher, hosted service, or native integration dependency.
Keep the provisional foundation read-only and evaluate it for later reuse; historical cloud architecture and remote rollout gates are not requirements.
Independent Fable specification review and user approval must precede detailed design; public licensing/publication remain separate user-owned release decisions.
open_product_questions: Linux+macOS is the proposed v1 platform scope, pending the user's already-asked platform preference.
The user must choose an open-source license before public release; this does not block specification review or design.
validation: Read assigned AGENTS.md and .pipeline/context.md in full.

Read final interoperability research and incorporated its generic interface, non-overwriting, trust, and support-evidence requirements.
Specification-only work: no project tests, dependencies, remote operations, source edits, live CLI installation, or graph generation.
next_gate: Fable specification review, resolution of findings, then user approval of the reviewed product specification.
